raw: 11.1 Geospatial Intelligence Fundamentals: IMINT, GEOINT, Mapping[^57]
teaching_note: Imagery interpretation concerns what an image supports; mapping locates representations in a reference system; GEOINT integrates imagery and geospatial information to assess spatial relationships. Coordinates need a declared coordinate reference system, datum and uncertainty, while a sharp image can still be poorly registered. MCRP 2-10B.4 is the GEOINT support manual, not a general reconnaissance manual [@ageint057]; doctrine describes a practice and does not validate a particular image interpretation.
title: Geospatial Intelligence Fundamentals: IMINT, GEOINT, Mapping

teaching_note: A body of knowledge organizes competencies such as remote sensing, geospatial data management and visualization; it is not evidence that an analyst has mastered them [@ageint058]. Diagnose a map by asking whether a reader can recover the coordinate system, scale, time coverage and missing-data treatment. Competency coverage and measured interpretation accuracy require different evidence.
title: GEOINT Essential Body of Knowledge (USGIF)

raw: 11.3 Commercial Satellite Platforms: Maxar, Planet, Sentinel-1/2[^59]
teaching_note: The raw inherited heading groups unlike providers: Maxar and Planet are commercial names, whereas Sentinel-1/2 belong to the Copernicus programme, not a commercial platform family. Compare supplied scenes by acquisition time, sensor modality, ground sampling, usable coverage and licence, not brand alone. The cited library is a discovery catalogue, not a primary specification for any platform's current resolution or revisit performance; such numerical claims remain unknown here.
title: Commercial Platforms and Public Programmes: Maxar, Planet, Sentinel-1/2

raw: 11.4 Change Detection and Pattern-of-Life Imagery Analysis
teaching_note: In a completed synthetic scene pair with matching sensor, grid scale, processing, illumination and clear coverage, a fictional shed edge is at pixel 40 in A and 43 in B, while three fixed markers also shift by +3 pixels. Registering B by those markers removes all shed displacement, yielding 'no resolved shed movement'; a variant with edge 46 leaves a 3-pixel residual, but a supplied ±2-pixel bound per image permits a ±4-pixel worst-case difference and the movement conclusion still stops. In a changed-feature control with edge 49, the corrected residual is 6 pixels and exceeds that bound, supporting a resolved positional difference under these assumptions, not object identity or intent. Removing markers makes registration unknown; cloud, season, sensor or resolution incompatibility likewise requires 'not comparable', not automatic confidence from freshness or source count. A thumbnail is no independent acquisition, publication time does not date the observed change, and two snapshots cannot establish a person's routine. USGIF's framework distinguishes registration, error and cross-sensor correction, but does not validate this author-defined exercise or supply a universal acceptable threshold [@ageint058].
title: Change Detection and Pattern-of-Life Imagery Analysis

raw: 11.5 GEOINT in Counterinsurgency and Strike Operations
teaching_note: This inherited operational heading is studied as a limit on inference, not as targeting instruction. A visible structure, vehicle-like shape or spatial association does not establish identity, hostile intent, civilian status or lawful authority to act; missing coverage is not proof of absence. The NGA mission page and analytic standards do not supply targeting authority or validate an operational decision, and this course excludes surveillance, live locations and strike support.
title: GEOINT in Counterinsurgency and Strike Operations

raw: 11.6 DoD GEOINT Accreditation and Training Standards[^60]
teaching_note: Separate programme accreditation, professional certification, a training requirement and accuracy on a particular task. Read a supplied dated manual extract for the institution, role and requirement it actually governs; neither the manual title nor course completion establishes certification. Current applicability or supersession remains unknown unless a dated authoritative issuance is supplied.
title: DoD GEOINT Accreditation and Training Standards

teaching_note: The cited title is Geospatial Intelligence Support to Operations [@ageint057]. Distinguish a doctrinal product category and its intended audience from the observations needed to populate that product. When a classroom packet lacks sensor metadata or a common spatial reference, report the missing input instead of borrowing certainty from the manual's authority.
title: MCRP 2-10B.4: USMC GEOINT Manual

raw: 11.8 AI-Assisted Satellite Image Analysis: Object Detection and Chronolocation
teaching_note: A detector score is a model output, not a calibrated probability of identity, activity or intent; retain model version, input derivative, class definition and threshold. In a fictional held-out answer sheet for model M1, squares S1/S2 are labelled present and S3/S4 absent, while thresholded predictions are present/present/present/absent: this gives two true positives, one false positive and one true negative on these four fixtures only. The S3 false detection prevents an 'every detection is real' conclusion, and duplicate crops cannot enlarge the independent evaluation set; no live model was evaluated or real-world accuracy established. Chronolocation concerns acquisition time, not upload time, and an uncalibrated clock or ambiguous shadows leaves the time interval unresolved. Resampling and an AI caption are transformations, not new observations or independent corroboration.
title: AI-Assisted Satellite Image Analysis: Object Detection and Chronolocation

teaching_note: A geospatial resource catalogue aids discovery, but linked tools and datasets retain their own provenance, versions, licences and known limits [@ageint059]. Distinguish a catalogue entry from the source scene, and preserve the exact scene identifier plus all cropping, reprojection and enhancement steps. A reachable link establishes neither factual truth nor permission for reuse; no external retrieval is required for these exercises.
title: Open-Source Geospatial Intelligence Library
